title: 2009 Portuguese legislative election
summary: The election of 27 September 2009 returned the Socialists to office without the majority they had held since 2005, ninety-seven seats of two hundred and thirty. The government that followed spent eighteen months legislating austerity packages through an Assembly that did not owe it a majority, and in March 2011 the fourth of them was rejected by every opposition party at once; the prime minister resigned and, six weeks later, asked the European Union and the International Monetary Fund for assistance. It is in the atlas as the arithmetic behind the request of 2011: a minority government, a deficit the markets had stopped funding, and a parliament that would not carry the measures either way.
